external_engines.title: Other Magic: The Gathering AIs & Engines (Research Survey, Nov 2026)
external_engines.note: No universal cross-engine MTG Elo ladder exists yet because each engine implements its own card scripting and rules interface. This survey compares the strongest publicly documented MTG game-playing AIs by architecture, card coverage, search depth, fairness, and practical speed/cost.

entries.name: Playmat AI (Phase 4 Neural ISMCTS)
entries.method: Transformer (2.05M-10.10M) + BGE-small card-text embeddings + Perfect-Info Oracle distillation + Multi-tree Gumbel-ISMCTS (fpu_vnode + MCTS-Solver)
entries.strengths: Beats omniscient heuristic search by up to +137 Elo and wins #1 on 38 strictly unseen OOD decks; 94% on tactics@4.
entries.limits: Card pool covers Pioneer/Standard and growing; 1v1 focus (multiplayer stays on Java).

entries.name: Playmat Rust Search (host@s6)
entries.method: Whole-turn playouts (extra_turns=1) + L2 logistic fitted evaluation (244 card weights) + declarative Playbooks for Ranked bots
entries.strengths: 100x+ faster than Java XMage MAD while outscoring it vs random (41-6-1 vs 37-9-2); instant browser play.
entries.limits: Beaten by Playmat's neural ISMCTS by 86-137 Elo on constructed@2.

entries.name: Gemini Decision 1 (Google Decisions API)
entries.method: Single-prefill calibrated choice model (POST /v1beta/decisions, 0 output tokens, normalized probabilities over legal actions)
entries.strengths: 11-14x faster and ~100x cheaper than generative reasoning LLMs; scored 1194 Elo (+194 over random) on constructed@2 duels and 8/16 (50%) on pro-decisions@1 with zero fallbacks.
entries.limits: No multi-turn tree search or thinking tokens; trails Playmat neural/search models on full duels and trails reasoning LLMs (Gemini 3.5 Flash 14/16, GPT-5.2 13/16) on multi-step stack puzzles.

entries.name: XMage Java MAD AI (ComputerPlayer7)
entries.method: Server-side minimax / MAD search over stack & priority with GameStateEvaluator2
entries.fairness: Sees hidden cards in default simulation
entries.speed_cost: 1.6 s p99 / 8.6-12 s CPU per game | $0 / game
entries.strengths: Broadest multiplayer/Commander & full-card support; strong local stack evaluation.
entries.limits: Heavy CPU cost per game, shallow multi-turn lookahead, no learned policy or belief tracking.

entries.name: Forge AI (Card-Forge)
entries.method: Per-card canPlayAI() scripts, AiHints, threat heuristics, and per-creature combat loops
entries.speed_cost: Fast on simple boards; slows on wide token boards | $0 / game
entries.strengths: Widely regarded as the best practical PvE MTG engine for sheer card coverage, drafts, and aggro/midrange decks.
entries.limits: Evaluates cards mostly in isolation; no multi-turn tree search or learned generalization; weak on control/combo without hand-coded hints.

entries.name: Magarena AI
entries.method: Expectimax & Monte Carlo Tree Search (Melvin Zhang MCTS) with hand-crafted MagicScore
entries.strengths: Historically regarded as the strongest classical lookahead AI among open-source engines thanks to its pruned, search-friendly ruleset.
entries.limits: Much smaller card pool, simplified rules, no neural networks or cross-card text generalization.

entries.name: MageZero (WillWroble)
entries.method: AlphaZero-style RL + MCTS decomposing MTG into single-deck environments
entries.strengths: Clean open-source AlphaZero framework on full XMage rules; proves focused deck-local RL works without LLM API costs.
entries.limits: Trains per-deck specialists rather than a universal cross-deck / zero-shot OOD model.

entries.name: MTG-Causal-RL (Academic, 2026)
entries.method: Causal Graph-Factored Advantage PPO (CGFA-PPO) over 3,077-dim partial obs + Structural Causal Model
entries.fairness: Partial observation with masked discrete actions
entries.strengths: Targets explicit causal credit assignment (e.g., holding mana for counterspells) and cross-archetype transfer.
entries.limits: Simplified Gymnasium environment rather than a full 14,000+ card rules engine.

entries.name: Frontier LLMs via MCP (mage-bench)
entries.method: Claude Opus 4.6, GPT-5.2, Gemini 3 Pro, DeepSeek V3.2 piloting full XMage games via structured tool calls
entries.strengths: Zero-shot understanding of any card ever printed, including multiplayer Commander politics and novel combos.
entries.limits: Orders of magnitude slower and costlier per game than dedicated RL/MCTS; still commits occasional tactical/state blunders.

entries.name: MTG Arena Sparky
entries.strengths: Fast, polished onboarding experience inside the official client.
entries.limits: Universally considered the weakest MTG bot; frequently miscalculates combat and removal timing.

llm_leaderboard.title: Strongest Frontier LLMs on Magic: The Gathering (mage-bench Season 1)
llm_leaderboard.scale_note: mage-bench Elo is computed strictly among 35 LLMs playing each other on XMage via MCP (1v1 & multiplayer). It is NOT on the same numeric scale as Playmat's Archbench Elo. Showing cost and thinking time per game alongside Elo highlights the trade-off between general-purpose LLMs and specialized neural game engines.
llm_leaderboard.other_benchmarks_note: Other public MTG LLM benchmarks show the same frontier split: on ManaBench (picking the optimal 60th card for a 59-card tournament deck), OpenAI o3 leads near 63% and Claude 3.7 Sonnet near 49.5%, while unassisted open-weight models like Llama 3.3/4 hover near 20-27% (random is 16.7%). On MTG Bench (engineless turn simulation via MCP), even top frontier models still suffer irreversible state-tracking errors without a rules engine.

suites.about: One-on-one duels with the 42 Pioneer and Standard school decks. Deal i is deck i % n against deck (i % n + 1 + i / n % (n - 1)) % n, shuffled with seed i, the first deck's seat starting on even deals (AiSpeedBenchTest's pairings). Each deal is played twice per pair of entrants, seats swapped. Changing a deck, the pairings or the turn cap makes a new version.

One-on-one duels with the 42 Pioneer and Standard school decks. Deal i is deck i % n against deck (i % n + 1 + i / n % (n - 1)) % n, shuffled with seed i, the first deck's seat starting on even deals: the 1722 deals are every ordered pair of decks once. Both seats take London mulligans as their AI decides. Each deal is played twice per pair of entrants, seats swapped. Changing a deck, the pairings, the mulligans or the turn cap makes a new version.
Out-of-distribution generalization benchmark: all 38 engine-playable held-out decks from Modern (3), Limited (20), and Brawl (15) disjoint from constructed-2 (1406 ordered duplicate deals).
Curated competitive MTG tournament decision suite split across 4 categories (aggro_race, control_stack, combat_math, tempo_open_mana) as an uncheatable external benchmark.

Positions with one right line, seat 0 to find it. The entrant plays both seats from the given step. Goals: win (seat 0 wins before the turn `turns` after this one ends), survive (seat 0 is alive when the turn after `turns` more begins), remove (seat 1 no longer controls `card`), keep (seat 0 still controls `card`), life (seat 0 has at least `life`). Libraries are 20 of the seat's first basic land unless given. Changing a puzzle makes a new version.

Positions with one right line, seat 0 to find it. The entrant plays both seats from the given step. Goals: win (seat 0 wins before the turn `turns` after this one ends), survive (seat 0 is alive when the turn after `turns` more begins), remove (seat 1 no longer controls `card`), keep (seat 0 still controls `card`), life (seat 0 has at least `life`). Libraries are 20 of the seat's first basic land unless given. Changing a puzzle makes a new version. tactics@2 is tactics@1's 16 puzzles and 15 more (trample, flying and reach, pumps after blocks, exert, deathtouch blocks, counters and protection on the opponent's turn, and traps: a wrath when ahead, a removal spell that costs the last life).
Hard multi-step tactical puzzles (stack counter-wars, Spell Pierce baiting, Prowess+Trample math, hold-up protection, Sunfall vs Intervention, two-turn lethal clocks, Giant Growth traps).
Phase 3 tactical frontiers: Nash burn standoffs, double-counter stack wars, manland+pump math, unblocked-attacker tricks, exile vs indestructible, open-mana tempo, and lifelink/sheoldred timing.

constructed1_runs.note: RustAiGameTest, 48 games (deals 0-47, 20-turn cap) of the school decks against a RandomDriver human seat, 6 at a time; not comparable with the rust-engine entrants. The Rust rows count games that left the Rust AI partway (8 and 7, engine differences) and were finished by the Java AI.
